plan_item: 77.44.7.A — tablet hover and focus-visible lifecycle across editable PARTIAL element types
finding: The existing representative tablet state lifecycle did not establish interaction-state coverage across every Inspector-editable PARTIAL element type. The expanded matrix also exposed that decorative aria-hidden output must not become keyboard reachable just because focus styles are configured.
change: Added tests/browser/editor-inspector-tablet-state-partial-types.test.js. The browser fixture exercises real Inspector states.set controls and Canvas styles for tablet hover and focus-visible on all 44 editable PARTIAL types, plus the draft, reload, public, publish, responsive inheritance, reset, and undo/redo lifecycle. Public focus-visible assertions run only on elements whose rendered semantics permit keyboard focus; aria-hidden elements are separately asserted to have no tabindex. No runtime code changed.
coverage: 44 editable PARTIAL types; tablet hover/focus-visible Inspector command and Page Model keys; Canvas computed styles; draft Save remains unpublished; reload restores Inspector values; separate Publish applies tablet states; desktop styles remain isolated; mobile inherits tablet; tablet reset restores desktop; Undo/Redo; reset Save preserves published values and reset Publish removes overrides; aria-hidden content remains outside keyboard navigation.
initial_harness_failure: The first full matrix expected every node to receive :focus-visible output. Chromium showed the spacer is intentionally rendered aria-hidden and the public renderer correctly refuses to add it to keyboard navigation. The test was corrected to assert focus-visible behavior on keyboard-focusable semantics and explicitly preserve the decorative aria-hidden exclusion. No product defect was found; no runtime fix was appropriate.
